tts_summary:
Good morning. Here's your Monday September 21st market briefing.

Futures are rallying to start the week — S&P up about 49 points or 65 basis points, Nasdaq up 110 basis points, and small caps up roughly 47 basis points. Europe is up 85 to 120 basis points, Asia closed broadly higher with the Hang Seng up 1.18% and Korea up 1.65%. Treasuries have a bid with yields down 2 to 3 basis points across the curve.

Here's the thing — the rally is a bit confounding because nearly all the weekend news flow was net negative. Houthis dramatically escalated missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia. Ukraine launched its largest drone strike on Russia yet. And a wave of troubling AI headlines dropped after Friday's close — delayed Anthropic IPO, underwhelming Anthropic 2027 revenue projections, OpenAI burning through cash at a rate that implies roughly 280 billion dollars in negative free cash flow through 2030, and Oracle's Project Jupiter data center debt hitting a wall with lenders.

So what's driving the strength? One word: diplomacy. The UN General Assembly runs September 22nd through the 28th in New York, and markets are betting that proximity of world leaders — including Iran's president — creates conditions for at least some de-escalation in the Middle East. Trump signaled he would be open to meeting Iran's president. He also reportedly called off air strikes against the Houthis at the last minute Sunday night after pushback from his inner circle. Add in Thursday's Trump-Xi summit, which could yield modest tariff reductions on about 30 billion dollars worth of goods, and you have two potential diplomatic catalysts this week.

On rates and the Fed — monetary policy is still firmly hawkish. The market has roughly 33 basis points of hikes priced in over the Fed's final two meetings of the year, with 50-50 odds at the October 28th meeting. Kashkari and Schmid both warned over the weekend that inflation is running hot beyond just energy. Meanwhile Treasury is planning to issue over a trillion dollars in T-bills over the next 12 months, pushing short-term debt above its own 20% target — a structural supply headwind for rates markets.

On the company side, Disney's parks business is outperforming its peers, defying the broader theme park traffic slowdown through price promotions and bundled packages — a positive read for that segment. Novo Nordisk is selling off in Europe after disappointing investors at its analyst day by failing to provide specific financial targets. Oracle continues to face negative pressure around its New Mexico data center debt struggles. And Paramount is in advanced settlement talks with California's attorney general over the Warner Bros. Discovery merger — potential divestitures including Comedy Central are on the table but a deal isn't done yet.

Brent crude is sliding 170 basis points to around 102 dollars, which is the most important macro variable to watch. If Middle East diplomacy gains any traction this week, an outsized oil decline becomes the most powerful bull catalyst in the market — lower energy means lower yields, less hawkish Fed policy, margin relief, and better consumer confidence. That's the entire bull thesis in one sentence.

The bear case is that the geopolitical situation remains deeply unstable, the AI infrastructure trade is under real pressure, global monetary policy is tightening in sync, and UN General Assembly optimism may simply be wishful thinking. Nothing major on the calendar today — the key events build through the week into PMIs Wednesday and the Trump-Xi summit Thursday. Stay nimble.
